title: ConfigError variants wrap String, losing structured fields
description: Both smtp/config.rs and reader/config.rs define ConfigError { Io(String), Parse(String), Validation(String) }. The String variants bury all structured information (field name, offending value, constraint) in a human-readable message. A caller that wants to retry only on I/O errors can match the Io variant, but a caller that wants to extract the failing field name or offending value from a Validation error cannot — the string must be parsed. Idiomatic Rust uses structured fields: Validation { field: &'static str, message: String } or a dedicated per-case variant. Additionally, both error types are identical — they could share a single definition in stoa-core or a common config-error crate to avoid divergence. The Display format using captured identifiers ({msg}) is correct Rust 1.58+ style; no issue there.
